from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Binary Language", [
            "Binary systems use only two digits: zero and one.",
            "Each position represents an increasing power of two.",
            "Four bits can represent numbers from zero to fifteen.",
            "Binary is the language of all modern computers."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        bits = Text("001", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(bits, 'C3')

        self.place_at_grid(bits_new, 'C3')

        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The puzzle has three rods and stacked discs.", 
                         "Move one disc at a time between rods.", 
                         "Never place a larger disc on a smaller one.", 
                         "The goal is moving all discs to another rod."]
        self.setup_layout("The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Puzzle
        # 3 Rods
        rods = VGroup(*[Line(DOWN*1, UP*1, color=GRAY) for _ in range(3)])
        self.place_at_grid(rods, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        # Rod Labels
        labels = VGroup(*[Text(label, font_size=24) for label in ["A", "B", "C"]])
        for i, l in enumerate(labels):
            l.next_to(rods[i], DOWN, buff=0.1)
            self.add(l)
        
        # 3 Discs
        discs = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w, height=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=1) 
                         for w, color in [(1.5, RED), (1.0, GREEN), (0.5, BLUE)]])
        discs.arrange(UP, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(discs, 'D2', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(rods), FadeIn(discs))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Highlight largest disk
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(discs[0], color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Animate move of largest disk to tower C (simplified)
        self.play(discs[0].animate.move_to(rods[2].get_center() + DOWN*0.8))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Moves to Binary Codes", [
            "We label moves from one to two power n.",
            "Binary digits map directly to disc moves.",
            "The lowest set bit determines which disc moves.",
            "Mapping Table"
        ])
        
        # Color definitions for animations
        c1 = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        c2 = "#FF00FF" # Magenta
        c3 = "#808080" # Grey
        
        # Table placeholders
        table = VGroup(
            Text("Move | Binary | Disc", font_size=24),
            Text("1 | 001 | 1", font_size=20, color=c1),
            Text("2 | 010 | 2", font_size=20, color=c2),
            Text("3 | 011 | 1", font_size=20, color=c1)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_in_area(table, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(table))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Logic representation
        disk_label = Text("Disc 1", color=c1)
        bit_label = Text("Bit 0", color=c1)
        self.place_at_grid(disk_label, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(bit_label, 'C5')
        
        line = Line(disk_label.get_right(), bit_label.get_left(), color=c3)
        self.play(FadeIn(disk_label), FadeIn(bit_label), Create(line))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Binary Direction Rule", [
            "Smallest discs follow a strict cyclic pattern.",
            "Larger discs move based on binary parity rules.",
            "This ensures the puzzle is always solved correctly."
        ])

        # Define rule indicators
        zero_rule = Text("0 = Move Right", color="#00FF00")
        one_rule = Text("1 = Move Left", color="#FF0000")
        rules = VGroup(zero_rule, one_rule).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        # Place in a clearly defined area on the right (B3 to D5)
        self.place_in_area(rules, 'B3', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(rules)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(zero_rule.animate.set_color("#00FF00"), one_rule.animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Simulating movement of a disc using primitive
        disc = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(disc, 'F3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(disc)
        self.play(disc.animate.move_to(self.grid['F5']), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Binary Language
sections.content: Introduce binary as a base-2 system. Explain that just as decimal uses 10 digits (0-9), binary uses only 0 and 1, where each position represents a power of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8...).
sections.example: Visual: A row of 4 light bulbs. Each bulb represents a bit. Bulb ON = 1, Bulb OFF = 0. Show how 1011 in binary equals 8+0+2+1 = 11 in decimal.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle
sections.content: Define the classic puzzle: 3 rods and n discs of different sizes. Rules: Move one disc at a time, never place a larger disc on a smaller one. The goal is to move the full stack to a target rod.
sections.example: Visual: 3 discs on Peg A. Animation shows the sequence of moves required to shift the stack to Peg C, emphasizing the recursive nature of the puzzle.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to Binary Codes
sections.content: Explain the surprising link: If we number the moves from 1 to 2^n - 1, the disc to be moved corresponds to the position of the lowest set bit in the binary representation of the move number.
sections.example: Visual: A table comparing Move Number (1-7), its Binary form (001, 010, 011...), and the disc to move (Disc 1, 2, 1, 3...). Use a character, 'Robo-Solver', pointing at the specific disc for each step.

sections.title: The Binary Direction Rule
sections.content: Define the direction of the moves based on binary state. For odd discs, moves go in a specific cycle; for even discs, the opposite cycle.
sections.example: Visual: 'Disk-o-Bot' moves Disc 1 (the smallest) clockwise among pegs, while larger discs follow a fixed parity rule based on their binary index, ensuring the puzzle is solved automatically.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Synthesize the concept: The puzzle is a physical manifestation of a binary counter. This logic is fundamental to recursive programming and algorithm complexity analysis.
sections.example: Visual: A final graphic showing a computer processor's clock cycle (0s and 1s) evolving into the movement of Hanoi discs, demonstrating how counting sequences drive mechanical movement.
